reasons: F07, F01, F02: the filing already contains a restatement of prior periods together with a material weakness in IT general controls, so the control environment that produces the numbers is shown to be unreliable

F03, F23: the company went public through a SPAC or reverse merger within 3 years and no auditor attestation on ICFR is required, so there is less outside checking of a new public-company reporting process
R04, R18, R01, R11: sales more than doubled (SGI 2.29), but receivables grew 83 percentage points faster than sales and DSRI is 1.36, which fits aggressive or early revenue recognition
F10: channel return rights or bill-and-hold arrangements exist, a known way to pull revenue forward in wholesale distribution, and this lines up with the receivables build-up (R18)
R09, R17: the Beneish M-score of -0.35 is well above the -1.78 threshold and the Dechow F-score of 1.1 is above 1.0, so both composite models flag likely manipulation
R03, R13: asset quality deteriorated sharply (AQI 2.74) and soft assets make up 72% of total assets, which leaves room for capitalising costs and for judgement-driven balances
R02: gross margin fell a lot (GMI 1.86), so margin pressure alongside rapid growth adds pressure to manage earnings
R19, R15: operating cash flow is only 0.64x net income while ROA improved (+0.12), so reported earnings are not fully backed by cash
F21, R16, F26: a capital raise during the year or planned (securities issued) and an emphasis on non-GAAP measures give a motive to present results favourably

Mitigating: F04, F05, F06, F14, F15, F16, F17, F19: no going concern doubt, no auditor change or disagreement, stable CEO/CFO, no SEC inquiry or litigation, no covenant problems; R07 leverage fell and R08/R10 accruals are negative, which tempers the score somewhat
